reason: The only offered combination assembles the lenses for observing the sky.
expectation: I expect a telescope that can be used to examine the Moon, Jupiter and Venus.

effect: The telescope is ready for the three observations; their interpretation will still need comparison.
reaction: The distinction between magnification and interpretation is useful.
reason: The changing lunar shadows can be compared with shadows on rough ground to address the Moon’s surface.
expectation: I expect the shadow pattern to support a rough rather than smooth lunar surface.

alternatives.reason: Jupiter’s nearby points could test whether everything circles Earth, but I chose to examine the Moon first.

effect: The lunar shadows support a rough surface and challenge a strict division between perfect heavens and imperfect Earth.
reaction: The comparison with earthly shadows makes the inference clear.
reason: The points staying near Jupiter may show that some bodies orbit something other than Earth.
expectation: I expect the changing positions to support the interpretation that Jupiter has orbiting companions.

alternatives.reason: Venus’s phases could test sky models too, but Jupiter’s companions address the next goal directly.

effect: Jupiter’s moons show that not everything orbits Earth directly, though they do not establish that Earth moves.
reaction: That limit on the observation is a useful distinction.
reason: The only remaining combination addresses the Venus phases goal.
expectation: I expect observations over several months to reveal Venus’s changing phases and their implications for sky models.

effect: Venus’s full range of phases gives sky models another observation they must explain; the chapter is complete.
reaction: The result is clear, though I would have liked a comparison of how different models account for the phases.

mostWorthwhile.text: Jupiter’s moons were most worthwhile: they challenge the idea that everything circles Earth directly, while showing why that alone does not prove Earth moves.

leastWorthwhile.text: Assembling the telescope was straightforward and less interesting than interpreting its observations, though it set them up.

surprise.text: The lunar shadows connected familiar shadows on rough ground to a challenge to the supposed perfection of the heavens.

arbitrary.text: Nothing felt purposeless; the offered combinations made each observation’s goal apparent, though they did not require discovering compatibility.

continue.text: Yes. I would be interested in seeing how competing sky models explain Venus’s phases, especially since this chapter stops short of comparing them.
